# sentin8.new  -  Repository-Split Backlog (RS)

Single backlog for the repository-split effort and its follow-ups. The
designs of record are `design/sentin8-repository-split-design.md` (RS) and
`design/sentin8-sdk-dependency-cleanup-design.md` (SDD). The original
monorepo (`../sentin8/`) is read as the source of truth for RS and never
modified; SDD executes against `sentin8.new/` directly.

## Conventions

- **Priority**: everything here is `P0` for this effort (the split is the
  current program). Ordering is by build order (RS §2.5, SDD §3), not
  priority.
- **Estimate**: `S` ≤ 1 day · `M` ≤ 3 days · `L` > 3 days.
- **IDs**: `RS-*` (split), `SD-*` (SDK dependency-direction cleanup +
  dissolution, per SDD). Defect classes fixed in the move are referenced
  as D1 - D8 (RS §3); SDD owner decisions as D1 - D9 (SDD §1.4).

| ✅ RS-12 | Contributor copyright attribution renamed to the owning unit: `Copyright Contributors to the {Brand} Project` → `Copyright Contributors to the {Brand}:{Leaf}` in all 98 repos / 2190 tracked files (source headers, NOTICE, LICENSE, configs)  -  platform `Sentin8:Auth`/`Sentin8:SDK`/…, vertical services `Bank8:Ledger`/`Hotel8:PMS`/…, groups + root keep the bare brand (`Bank8`, `Sentin8`). Docs-canonical casing harvested from the DESIGN docs (BFF, FDX, DB, SDK, Acme, Dash); NOTICE prose line (`developed by the {Brand} Project`) unchanged by design. | S | RS §2.3.1 |
| ✅ RS-13 | `authors` field dropped from every Cargo.toml (153 manifests, 68 repos): the field is optional, unused by any consumer, and duplicated identity already carried by the SPDX headers + NOTICE  -  direct literals, `authors.workspace = true` inherits, and `[workspace.package]` definitions removed together so no dangling inherits remain. `cargo metadata` verified clean across all manifest shapes. | S | RS §4.5 |

Cargo git-dep pins, `repository=` fields, Cargo.lock git sources (org URLs + new commit revs), NOTICE project URLs, packaging Homepage/Vcs-Git/Documentation, design-doc examples, and the root `.gitignore` (`/health8/`) updated in the same change; `sentin8-ai`'s stale `cron-sdk-v0.1.0` pin normalized to `v0.2.0`. `cargo fetch` verified green across all orgs (trade8-desk, bank8-fdx, bill8-payments). `health8` intentionally untouched (stays at `lmgc-code/health8`). | L | RS §2.3.1 |

| ID | Story | Est | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ DEVRESET-1 | Reset friction eliminated by splitting the reset's two planes: `dev-destroy.sh` becomes a PURE INFRA reset (stop fleet → compose `down -v` deleting both named volumes → `infra-tls` re-mint/reseed → compose up + ownership fix for fresh root-owned volumes + health-wait; no psql, no bootstrap, no enroll, no finalize, no `captain start`), and database convergence moves into the operator's normal flow - `make enroll` and the cold-boot `captain start` provision-on-boot pass both gain a bootstrap-if-needed step (`db bootstrap` auto-run when the `sys.platform_bootstrap` scout is absent) ahead of their existing idempotent enroll convergence, so `make stop` → reset → `make enroll` → `make start` works out of the box and each step is individually re-runnable. Root causes fixed in the same change: (a) auth's `init.sql` carried `//` comments inside a SQL migration (PostgreSQL syntax error at migration-1 apply) aborting the whole enroll; (b) enroll aborted wholesale on the first migration failure - now a fixed-point convergence loop defers and retries (ai seeds `stat.properties`), failing loudly only when no progress remains, and registers rows after SQL converges (m2m grants previously skipped on fresh DBs); (c) the inverted role search_path row-check never filled fresh service roles - every reset re-created roles with NO search_path and every unqualified query crash-looped (auth on `signing_keys`); (d) `make enroll` derives its fragment list from `service-registration.json` presence (the stale hardcoded list class). | M | sentin8-cli DESIGN §4.9a |
| ✅ COREAP-1 | Core appliance dev split-plane: a second compose project (`docker-compose.core.yml`) runs postgres + valkey + one "machine" container (captain + the 17 platform binaries, bind-mounted from the group target trees - no image build) with `SENTIN8_CAPTAIN_LOCAL_IP=127.0.0.1` and exactly four loopback-published entry ports (443/5432/6379/18000), so verticals run as host processes against an identical-to-today core (same DSNs, same `*.local.sentin8.dev` → 127.0.0.1 DNS); two captains share one Valkey with distinct machine identities; the CLI gains per-key transport routing for instance ops (appliance-ip keys → the appliance captain, UDS socket first, bearer-gated TCP fallback; enabled by `SENTIN8_CORE_APPLIANCE_IP`) and captain gains the locality guard (per-instance actions refused for keys whose ip is not its own - a remote key meant signaling an unrelated pid in the caller's namespace); `make core-up`/`core-down`/`core-logs` drive the appliance and `make start` refuses while it is up (double-boot guard); hand-off of a core service between the appliance and the host is stop-instance + start (verified live both directions, traffic follows the registry round-robin through the in-container proxy). Live-E2E hardening folded in: absolute-path compose binds (WSL gRPC-FUSE materializes relative binds as empty dirs), fresh-volume chown (the initdb EPERM class), `--infra-sans` SAN-coverage-aware leaf minting (bridge netns dials infra by compose name), writable secrets + mounted platform-CA dir (the appliance acme IS the platform CA), the host-UDS bind-mounted control socket (peer-cred lifecycle ops), and the entrypoint's host-path/host rewrites (`SENTIN8_PG_HOST`/`SENTIN8_VALKEY_HOST`, `DATABASE_URL`/`VALKEY_URL`, per-service DSN fills for the SDK's hardcoded-localhost fallbacks). Verified: 17-instance fleet Active in-container; host→appliance :443 healthy; auth hand-off docker→host→docker with zero traffic loss. | L | sentin8-captain DESIGN §11.11, sentin8-cli DESIGN §4.3, group DESIGN §3.3 |

SD-8 (verification).

| ID | Story | Est | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| SD-1 | `sentin8-sdk` plane: shield `stat_emit` transport → membus `stat:telemetry` Pub/Sub (drop stat-client dep, drop `{leaf}-policy` M2M workload, keep the public emit API); facade drops all service modules + legacy `auth.rs`/`db.rs` hand-rolled clients; `sentin8-registration` gains `ScheduleDecl` + `schedules` section; SDK workspace members shrink to the 24 shared-plane crates; docs refreshed same change. | L | SDD §2.1 - 2.4 |
| SD-2 | Declarative schedules plumbing: `sentin8-cli vertical enroll` reads `--section=schedules` and upserts `cron.schedules` (idempotent, `schedule_type` unique per (env, domain)); `service-registration.json` gains `schedules`. | M | SDD §2.4, §4.1 |
| SD-3 | Root-service timers: auth jwks-rotation and acme renewal-sweep delete their boot-time `CronClient` + M2M DCR blocks; auth gains an internal daily timer (03:00, 30-day staleness gate → in-process `jwks::rotate`); acme keeps its internal sweep loop only. | S | SDD §2.5 |
| SD-4 | Declarative schedule declarations: secrets (expiry, prune), ai (archive, reembed), bank8-payments (DEFAULT_SCHEDULES), bank8-registration (filing calendar), exchange8-gateway, exchange8-refdata add `schedules` sections and delete runtime registration code. | M | SDD §2.4 |
| SD-5 | Telemetry → MemBus: auth/ai/app/email8-mta `build_stat_client`+DCR plumbing deletes; emitters publish `stat:telemetry` frames via the SDK telemetry helper; stat `redis_sub.rs` worker gains the `stat:telemetry` subscription + frame decode + ingest path; bff tagging.rs test rewritten against the stat read surface. | L | SDD §2.3, §2.6 |
| SD-6 | SDK-crate dissolution (platform + verticals): 16 platform crates move into 11 owner repos, each owner gains a `sdk/` mini-facade (`sentin8-{svc}-sdk` package, `pub use` re-exports only); consumers re-pin owner git tags; bank8-ledger's hand-rolled `cron_client.rs` replaced by the cron mini-facade; import sweep across all consumer repos. **Vertical half refined by measurement (2026-10-04)**: trade8/exchange8/email8 SDKs are SHARED vertical planes (fixed/Price-Qty math, FIX/OUCH/ITCH protocols, IMAP/SMTP/ical, event contracts  -  every sibling service links them)  -  they STAY as `{vertical}-sdk` per the owner's stay/move boundary (shared-plane linkage, SDD-1); only per-service crates in bank8 (4 contracts), hotel8 (12 client/contracts), bill8 (9 contracts) dissolve into their owner repos. | L | SDD §3.1 - 3.5 |
| SD-6b | Vertical per-service crate dissolution follow-up: move bank8/hotel8/bill8 per-service contracts + clients into owner service repos (`sdk/` mini-facades), re-point the `bank8::`/`hotel8::`/`bill8::` facade imports, retire those three facade repos + crate names; trade8/exchange8/email8 SDKs stay (shared vertical planes). | L | SDD §3.4 |
| SD-7 | Packaging: vendored registry refreshes for mini-facade sources (per-owner-repo vendoring), `manifest.yaml` paths updated. | S | SDD §4.3 |
| SD-8 | Whole-tree verification: SDK build clean; starters; 17 platform services; vertical groups; fleet boot smoke (no `{leaf}-policy` DCR workloads, no cron self-registration logs, schedules present post-enroll); legacy-naming sweep greps clean. **Done 2026-10-04 (build layer): 17/17 platform + 43/43 vertical green; full-fleet boot smoke + legacy-sweep re-verification rides the nightly.** | M | SDD §6 |
| ✅ SD-10 | **Discovery refresh failure semantics  -  a failed/suspect registry scan wipes the in-memory service map (found live 2026-10-20 in the OIDF rig run).** `ServiceDiscovery::refresh` did `client.keys(GLOB).await.unwrap_or_default()`  -  a transient Valkey error yields an empty KEYS list and the previous map is REPLACED with an empty one: every service vanishes from discovery fleet-wide (callers see "ACME not resolved via service discovery" outages) until the next successful scan, and callers like the on-demand TLS cert fetch strand tenant hostnames (`tlsv1 alert access denied`). Live incident: auth's discovery map wiped during an ACME self-heal window → the cert tenant host could not be fetched even though ACME's registry row was healthy. Target state (crate doc "Refresh failure semantics"): a FAILED scan (KEYS/HGETALL error) keeps the previous map + logs an error; one unreadable hash is skipped, not fatal; an EMPTY scan result is REJECTED when the previous map is non-empty (the platform never runs with zero services  -  empty is indistinguishable from a partitioned scan) and accepted only when the map was already empty; `refresh_one` keeps the type's view on read failure. Pure seam `should_reject_empty_scan`/`total_instances` unit-tested. **Done 2026-10-20: fix + tests (14 green) in sentin8-sdk service-discovery.** | P0 | S | sentin8-sdk/core/service-discovery crate docs §"Refresh failure semantics"; live incident 2026-10-20 |
| ✅ SD-11 | **Per-tenant JWT signing algorithm (owner request 2026-10-20: "make SENTIN8_TLS_PQ_MODE settable per environment").** The env var is process-level; the TLS transport half must STAY process-level (the ClientHello key exchange completes before the SNI hostname  -  and therefore the tenant  -  is known; per-tenant TLS groups are physically impossible on one listening socket). The JWT signing half moves onto the security-profile plane: `security_profiles.signing_alg` (`MLDSA65` \| `RS256`, default `MLDSA65`, CHECK-constrained) resolved platform → org → env like the flags; `SigningKeys` loads BOTH algorithm key sets (verification already accepts both for rotation overlap) and signing picks the family per request at every mint site that resolves tenant context (ID token, access, refresh, JARM, logout token, SD-JWT credential); discovery advertises the caller's env-resolved `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported`; JWKS serves both families (kid-routed verifiers). Per-tenant KEYS are rejected (rotation/revocation surface ×N, no security gain at the JWT layer  -  the tenant boundary is the claim set, not the key). Acme cert families stay with the TLS transport mode. **Done 2026-10-21: column + resolution + sign_value_alg + all mint sites (code/refresh/device/CIBA/M2M/external/token-exchange) + discovery advertisement; both families provisioned at boot (JWKS serves MLDSA65+RS256); live-verified platform advertises MLDSA65 while the cert env advertises RS256 on the same process; 246 auth tests green. Companion SDK fixes shipped as sdk-v0.6.9 (discovery safety poll 60s→15s  -  poll must stay under the 30s health-freshness window; proxy upgraded onto it: the :443 edge terminates TLS for tenant hostnames and its stale binary stranded on-demand cert fetches).** | P1 | M | auth DESIGN §9a.9; owner decision 2026-10-20 |

(17/17 platform Rust repos + 43/43 vertical services green  -  trade8's stale

## Open (OIDF conformance program  -  the rig must run zero-skipped, zero-failed)

Design of record: `sentin8/sentin8-auth/DESIGN.md` §9a (certification
program + rig); runbook `sentin8/scripts/conformance/README.md`. Program
rule (owner decision 2026-10-21): **a SKIPPED conformance test is a
FAILED conformance test**  -  the suite skips exactly when discovery
declines to advertise a capability, which is a coverage hole, never a
pass (auth DESIGN §9a.10).

| ID | Story | Pri | Est | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLATADMIN-1 | **The `sentin8:sys:admin` role seed empties its own permissions, so NO user can ever be platform admin on a fresh apply (found live 2026-10-21 during the OIDF re-seed: the bootstrap admin's `GET /v1/o` failed `forbidden by policy` after the OIDF-SCOPE-1 greenfield reset).** `sql/init.sql` seeds the role twice with contradictory intent: the per-service block (line ~2221) seeds the full platform scope set, then the "platform super-user" block (line ~2334) OVERWRITES it with `ARRAY[]` ("scopes come from nested service-admin roles") - the later INSERT's `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` wins, so the live role is `{}`. But the nesting closure (dash:admin, auth:admin, db:admin, …) carries no role containing the literal `sentin8:sys:admin` scope (nor any sys:read-satisfying scope): the marker that `is_platform_admin()` matches (`sentin8or_auth.rs` - whose doc comment documents exactly the org:sys:admins group → org:sys:admin role → nested sys:admin role chain) and that the enforced scope-mirror policies permit on (`sentin8:sys:read`/`instances:read`/`org:admin` when `scopes.contains("sentin8:sys:admin")`) is unreachable for every principal. The earlier working DB only functioned because the operator's token predated the reset. Target state (auth DESIGN §3 "Platform-admin contract"): the super-user block seeds the role's OWN permissions as `ARRAY['sentin8:sys:admin']` (the marker) with service scopes still arriving via the nested service-admin roles; the duplicate contradictory seed at line ~2221 is left as the per-service granular set it coexists with (unique constraint means the LAST upsert defines the row - the super-user block is the authoritative one and now carries the marker). Verified by: fresh apply → `a@m.n` token scope contains `sentin8:sys:admin` → `sentin8-cli call sys GET /v1/o` 200. **Done 2026-10-21: seed fixed (marker scope restored, comment documents the contract); live role converged via the seed's own idempotent upsert; the CLI token re-minted through the device flow carries `sentin8:sys:admin` (verified by decoding the access token) and `GET /v1/o` returns 200; the conformance seed proceeds.** | P0 | S | auth `sentin8or_auth.rs:58` doc contract; live 403 finding 2026-10-21 |
| OIDF-SCOPE-1 | **The OIDC `address`/`phone` claim scopes are unimplemented, so the suite SKIPPED 3 of 15 Basic-OP tests (`oidcc-scope-address`, `oidcc-scope-phone`, `oidcc-scope-all`  -  verified live in the rig Mongo, plan `khiuQplorvoFp`).** Discovery hardcodes `scopes_supported = [openid profile email offline_access]` (oauth.rs discovery mint) and `claims_supported` carries no address/phone entries; the ID-token mint (`jwt.rs` `id_token_with_details`) gates only email/profile; userinfo returns neither and emits `email`/name unconditionally of the consented scope; the users table carries `phone` but no postal-address columns. Target state (auth DESIGN §9a.4/§9a.10): (1) `sql/init.sql` users gains the postal columns (`street_address`, `locality`, `region`, `postal_code`, `country`); (2) discovery advertises `openid profile email phone address offline_access` and the full `claims_supported` (adds `phone_number`, `phone_number_verified`, `address`); (3) the ID-token mint gains `include_phone_claims`/`include_address_claims` scope-gated params (same pattern as email/profile) and the OIDC `address` JSON object; every mint site (code exchange, CIBA, device ID-token paths) passes the user's phone + address data; the §5.5 `claims` selection narrows the new claims too; (4) userinfo scope-gates email/name/phone/address on the token's scope (currently unconditional  -  spec defect the suite checks) and serves the new fields; (5) DCR's `OIDC_BASELINE` adds `phone`/`address`; admin user create/update accepts + persists phone and postal address (the write surface the rig seed uses); (6) `conformance-seed.sh` registers clients with `scope: "openid profile email phone address offline_access"` and provisions the cert user's phone + address via the admin API. Verification: live discovery advertises the scopes; suite re-run shows the 3 tests PASSED, zero SKIPPED; auth unit+integration tests green. **Done 2026-10-21 (with the companion conformance fixes the run surfaced  -  all design-first per AGENTS): schema columns + discovery/claims advertisement + scope-gated minting (code exchange/CIBA/device/userinfo with §5.5 selection narrowing) + DCR baseline + admin persistence + seed data; AND: tenant-aware issuer on every token mint (§4 - the suite's ValidateIdToken failed `Issuer mismatch`, a process-constant iss is un-certifiable per tenant); domain-AGNOSTIC issuer check per owner note (`https://auth.{env-domain}` is opaque - no `{env}.{org}.{tld}` structural parsing anywhere); userinfo gets GET+POST (§5.3.1 - 405 on post variants) with form-body bearer support and per-scope claim gating; RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 authorize-error REDIRECTS after client/redirect_uri validation (the response-type-missing test stalled on an inline 400); RFC 6749 §5.1 `Cache-Control: no-store` + `Pragma: no-cache` on token/introspect/revoke (edge middleware); RFC 6749 §5.2 JSON error bodies on ALL token-endpoint 4xx (codereuse failed on a text/plain 400); RFC 9101 §5 unsigned (`alg:none`) request objects accepted + advertised (2 SKIPPED tests re-run green; exp strictly-when-present); prompt/max_age semantics (§3.1.2.1: fresh-session silent reissue keeps `auth_time` = session created_at - the max-age pair failed on a second session minting a new auth_time); the PLATADMIN-1 seed split-defect (`sys:admin` role emptied by its second seed block - no principal could ever be platform admin); refresh-token CLIENT BINDING (SEC defect: a client-2 refresh token accepted by client 1 - bound at mint, compared at grant) and the RLS-bare-pool user fetches in the grant handlers (§4.3d - email minted as "" and the suite's standard-claims check failed); seed script: cert-tenant signup host, cert-host DCR (ops-host DCR landed clients in SYSTEM env), CIBA duplicate-grant fix, client idempotency cleanup, profile step, TLS warm-up; rig ingress platform-CA leaf (✅ OIDF-CERT-1); TLSHOLD-1 first-touch cert handshake HOLD (sdk-v0.6.11; the no-retry Java client took `access_denied` during the ~100ms on-demand fetch). FINAL LIVE RESULT 2026-10-21: **all 35 OIDC-Core-Basic-OP tests reach terminal PASSED/WARNING/REVIEW  -  zero FAILED, zero INTERRUPTED, zero SKIPPED** (REVIEW = the two screenshot-upload confirmations, expected at submission). The remaining §9a.5 profiles (Config/Dynamic/Logout/FAPI/CIBA/wallet/IDA) ride OIDF-PROFILES-1. Auth 249/249 tests green throughout.** | P0 | M | auth DESIGN §9a.4/§9a.10; live rig finding 2026-10-21 (3 SKIPPED); owner no-skip rule |
| ✅ OIDF-CERT-1 | **The suite's front-channel callback surface is untrusted in the operator browser, so all 11 browser-driven tests INTERRUPT (`ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` on the plan tab; `oidcc-display-page` WAITING→FAILED).** The suite nginx image hardcodes a self-signed `CN=localhost` cert; the platform's Acme root CA is already in the OS trust store (curl to `auth.*.sentin8.dev` verifies without `-k`), so the target state is to serve the rig's own hostnames (`localhost.emobix.co.uk`) from a platform-CA-signed leaf: `make conformance-up` mints/copies a leaf for the suite hostname and the compose nginx service bind-mounts it over the image's `/etc/ssl/certs/nginx-selfsigned.crt` + key paths (no image rebuild). Then re-run the INTERRUPTED tests and complete `oidcc-display-page`'s by-design manual confirmation. **Done 2026-10-21: `--ensure-infra-tls` mints `infra-tls/conformance-suite-server.crt/.key` (CN `conformance-suite`, SANs `localhost.emobix.co.uk` + loopbacks, 90-day renewal window) as a new `EnsureReport.conformance_suite_cert` field (auth DESIGN §9a.2 step 1b + runbook §1 refreshed same-change); `make conformance-up` gates on the pair's presence (`make infra-tls` hint) and copies it into the compose context; the nginx service bind-mounts it read-only over the image's hardcoded paths; acme rebuilt warning-free; rig restarted  -  live-verified: `openssl` shows the leaf served with `CN=Sentin8 Local Development Intermediate CA` issuer, `curl` WITHOUT `-k` returns 302 on `:8443`, the plan page (`plan=khiuQplorvoFp`) loads in the browser with zero cert interstitials (was ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID). NOTE: the auth-schema greenfield reset (OIDF-SCOPE-1) wiped the suite's registered DCR clients  -  `make conformance-seed` re-registers them once the operator re-signs in (`sentin8-cli signin`, device flow), then the INTERRUPTED/scope tests re-run.** | P1 | S | rig runbook §1; live rig finding 2026-10-21 (11 INTERRUPTED, 1 WAITING) |
| OIDF-PROFILES-1 | **Only the Basic-OP plan has ever been run (6 attempts in the rig Mongo; zero runs of Config, Dynamic, RP-Initiated/Back-Channel Logout, FAPI 2 SP/Message-Signing, FAPI 1 Advanced, CIBA Poll/Ping, OID4VCI, OID4VP, IDA).** No defect  -  runbook execution: after OIDF-SCOPE-1 + OIDF-CERT-1 land green, run each remaining §9a.5 profile plan in the suite (alias `sentin8-local`, per-profile security-profile switch per the seed script), export logs to `.tmp/conformance/results/`, zero FAILED/INTERRUPTED/SKIPPED per profile. | P1 | L | auth DESIGN §9a.1/§9a.5 |

## Open (Fleet runtime  -  audit-journal provisioning, email8-mta leak, idle CPU)

Design of record: `sentin8/design/sentin8-audit-journal-provisioning-design.md`
(AUDJOUR); the SDK audit crate's `audit_journal_sql(schema)` is the single
DDL contract every init.sql mirrors (WARN-14's precedent). Found via the
2026-10-16 memory-leak investigation: the fleet at 33GB used / 15GB swap
turned out to be one real per-process heap leak (email8-mta) plus a
warning storm (~39,700 WRNs/day) caused by the audit-journal pusher
retrying missing/stale tables every 7s forever.

| ID | Story | Pri | Est | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ SIGNENROLL-2 | **The enroll inventories predated `sign`: the root `Makefile` enroll list and `sentin8-cli/src/db.rs` `platform_pg_ident_rows()` (the CLI-embedded platform `pgm` census) both omitted `sign` - after any `.run/secrets` reset, `make enroll` re-wrote 40 identity rows and STILL left CN `m2m-sentin8:sign` unmapped; every cert-auth connection from `sentin8:sign` failed `certificate authentication failed for user "sentin8_sign_service"` (crash-loop 2026-10-27/28/29).** Fix: `platform_pg_ident_rows` gains `"sign"` (→ `sentin8_sign_service`); the census-convergence rule documented in DESIGN §3.2.2. | BUSNACKNULL-1 | **The bus's NACK retry path drops the event payload  -  every retried event is unreplayable.** Found 2026-10-16 while verifying PROVRLS-1's backlog drain: `POST /v1/nack` (bus handlers.rs) writes its retry record to the `bus:retry:{env}` zset with `"payload": Null` and `event_type: req.stream_family` (the stream family, not the event); when the reaper's retry-time arrives it re-ADDs a stream entry from that record  -  a retry ENVELOPE whose fields are `{event_type: "auth", payload: null, retry_of, retry_count}` instead of the original event. Consumers receive a frame that matches no handler (`event_type` is the family) with a null payload; the original `sentin8:auth:user:created` {user_id, email} is gone forever. Consequences: (1) any event that ever NACKs (transient failure) becomes an unreplayable tombstone  -  the email8:store provisioner's 2,240-entry PEL is entirely poisoned envelopes (retry_count=1, payload null); (2) consumers ACK the meaningless envelope (event_type mismatch → no-op success) so the stream looks drained while the work never happened; (3) the retry counter can never do its job. Target state: the NACK record must carry the FULL original entry (all fields incl. the payload, correlation id, idempotency key, publisher identity)  -  either copy the entry's fields into the zset member at NACK time, or store the message id and have the reaper re-XREAD the original entry from the stream by id (entries are never trimmed before the retry window). The reaper's re-ADD writes the original field set verbatim; the retry envelope keeps only `retry_of`/`retry_count` as ADDED fields, never replacing originals. Poisoned PELs are disposable (greenfield): after the fix, delete the `bus:retry:{env}` zsets and drain remaining null-payload entries by ACK. | P0 | M | bus handlers.rs nack (payload: Null at the zadd); bus reaper.rs retry re-ADD; live XREADGROUP proof 2026-10-16 (entries 1792018266374-0/1792018340617-0: event_type=auth, payload=null, retry_of=1792018229191-0); design/sentin8-provisioned-rls-and-telemetry-design.md §1.1 verification note |

| ✅ BUSCONNP-1 | **The bus's `POST /v1/consume` runs its blocking `XREADGROUP` on the SHARED command client while exchange8-oms/risk poll it in a 1s-block loop  -  a self-sustaining GLIDE-watchdog `SystemOverload` WARN storm (~29/min, 9.7k in one session, still firing).** Verified live 2026-10-17: glide-core 0.1.1's `timeout_watchdog` classifies any timeout as `SystemOverload` when >100 commands are process-globally registered (the bus holds ~197 idle SSE connections each parked in a 10s blocking read  -  the threshold is structurally exceeded); exchange8-oms/risk's `ConsumeRequest { block_ms: 1000, max_count: 500 }` loops issue the only short-deadline blocking reads, and glide derives their request timeout from the command itself (BLOCK 1000ms + 0.5s extension = `configured=1.5s`). ## Open (SIGN  -  core e-signature service: Sentin8:Sign)

Design of record: `sentin8/sentin8-sign/DESIGN.md` (the service repo
shipped in the same change). Program origin: the QES ceremony stub in
sentin8-auth named the bank8 vertical as its owner  -  an absolute-rule-1
violation in core platform docs; e-signature is a cross-vertical
platform capability (contract ceremonies in hotel8, account openings in
bank8, confirmations in trade8), so the ceremony engine is a core
platform service (Post-shaped: durable state machine + gateway seam +
outbox events), with verification primitives as an SDK crate so
consumers verify in-process on their hot paths.

## Open (OAPEC  -  OpenAPI coverage & drift: every served route documented)

Design of record: `design/sentin8-openapi-coverage-design.md` (OAPEC).
Found 2026-10-17 (owner: "server.rs has a lot more APIs than what the
OpenAPI reports in sites for each service"): the API reference pages on
every service site are rendered from the checked-in `docs/openapi.json`
dumps, and those dumps lag the routers massively  -  ~900 missing
(method, path) pairs across 33 spec-owning services, ~45 stale spec
paths, and trade8 (6) + exchange8 (14) services carry no OpenAPI
surface at all. Nothing enforces router↔spec equality; the drift-guard
test (OAPEC-1) is the durable enforcement, the per-service stories are
the one-time catch-up.

## Open (OC  -  OIDF certification program: local conformance + submission)

Design of record: `sentin8/sentin8-auth/DESIGN.md` §9a (conformance rig).
Scope (owner decision 2026-10-20): certify **everything the platform
implements except Front-Channel Logout and Implicit/Hybrid OP**  -  i.e.
OIDC Basic + Config + Dynamic OP, RP-Initiated + Back-Channel Logout,
FAPI 2 Security Profile + Message Signing, FAPI 1 Advanced, FAPI-CIBA
(poll + ping), OID4VCI issuer, OID4VP verifier, eKYC-IDA. The OIDF
conformance suite is free and runs **locally first** (docker,
`.tmp/conformance/`); fees are waived under the OIDF open-source project
certification policy at submission time. Build order: OC-1…OC-5
(protocol gaps) ∥ OC-8 (suite compatibility) → OC-6/Oc-7 (spec
alignment) → OC-9 (rig + run) → OC-10 (submission).

## Open (EU  -  openfin8-eu: the Berlin Group openFinance adapter, OBARCH-7)

Design of record: `openfin8/openfin8-eu/DESIGN.md` (OBARCH-7  -  the EU
deltas over the kernel) + `openfin8/openfin8-eu/BUSINESS.md` (§9 = the
acceptance criteria, the program's definition of done); kernel
contract: `openfin8/openfin8-core/DESIGN.md` (OBARCH-1); vertical
rollup: `openfin8/DESIGN.md` +
`design/sentin8-openfin8-vertical-split-design.md` (OBVERT  -  the
composition boundary). Current state: SKELETON  -  the shell boots
(`Sentin8Shell::new("openfin8:eu", "OPENFIN8_EU")`), the published-spec
drift guard is green (the CC BY 4.0 attribution present, zero
foreign-standard prefixes), and nothing else exists: empty `sql/`, a
service_type + telemetry-only registration fragment, no wire, no
ceremony. The heaviest adapter of the set (EU DESIGN status note):
three SCA interaction modes, no central directory, PSD3/FDA in
flight. IDs: `EU-*`.

Decided questions (EU DESIGN §8, carried into the stories): ship the
Berlin Group openFinance V2 wire now  -  PSD3/FDA lands as a follow-on
wire family behind the SAME adapter boundary (the KPI is absorbability
without a kernel rewrite); domestic variants (STET/FR, PolishAPI/PL,
Slovak BA) are customer-specific follow-ons on the UK-over-CA pattern,
NOT v1 scope; embedded SCA is config-gated (redirect is the mandatory
always-served approach).

Build order: EU-1 (skeleton identity) → EU-2 (consent + authorisation
model) → EU-3 (SCA ceremonies) → EU-4 (eIDAS + DCR) → EU-5 (PIS +
signing baskets) → EU-6 (AIS + PIIS) → EU-8 (e2e) → EU-7/EU-9
(extended services; publication + site parity).

## Open (UK  -  openfin8-uk: the OBL Read/Write API adapter, OBARCH-5)

Design of record: `openfin8/openfin8-uk/DESIGN.md` (OBARCH-5  -  the UK
deltas over the kernel) + `openfin8/openfin8-uk/BUSINESS.md` (§9 = the
acceptance criteria, the program's definition of done); kernel contract:
`openfin8/openfin8-core/DESIGN.md` (OBARCH-1); vertical rollup:
`openfin8/DESIGN.md`. Current state: SKELETON  -  the shell boots
(`Sentin8Shell::new("openfin8:uk", "OPENFIN8_UK")`), the publication
guard asserts the vendored OBL MIT notice, and nothing else exists:
empty `sql/`, a print-nothing registration stub, no wire, no ceremony.
Per the EU program's precedent (OBARCH-7): the first adapter with a
non-FDX wire  -  a new ceremony family (FAPI 1 Advanced), a new envelope
(`{Data, Links, Meta}`), detached JWS request/response signing, and the
intent-based consent model over the kernel's `awaiting_authorization`
state. IDs: `UK-*`.

Decided questions (UK DESIGN/BUSINESS, carried into the stories): the
served version is `OPENFIN8_UK_VERSION` (default `3.1.11`, `4.0.1`
configurable); OB Directory JWKS unavailability fails CLOSED (503,
never skip-verify); VRP v1 is the `vrp-basic` sweeping profile
(non-sweeping is a follow-on); file payments are a follow-on (the
Payments file pipeline exists; the OBL surface lands after the
domestic-payment core); the OBL conformance suite's operational run
(CI nightly vs pre-release) is an open business question, not a code
blocker.

Build order: UK-1 (skeleton identity + schema/registration) → UK-2
(the intent consent model) → UK-3 (the FAPI ceremony + JWS signing) →
UK-4 (the envelope codec + error semantics) → UK-5 (the AIS resource
surfaces) → UK-6 (the PIS surfaces + VRP) → UK-7 (CBPII + event
notifications) → UK-8 (the e2e journey) → UK-9 (publication + site
parity).
